what_its_for: This eye drop is used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is used to treat open-angle glaucoma (a condition where fluid builds up and raises pressure in the eye) and a condition called ocular hypertension (high eye pressure). Lowering eye pressure helps protect your vision and prevents damage to the optic nerve.
how_to_take: Use this medicine only in your eye(s) — never swallow it. Wash your hands thoroughly before using the drops. Tilt your head back and gently pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket. Hold the dropper tip above your eye and squeeze out one drop. Close your eye gently and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) with one finger for about 1 to 2 minutes. This helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces absorption into the rest of your body. Do not blink or rub your eye. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each different eye medicine. Remove contact lenses before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, eyelid, fingers, or any other surface to avoid contamination.
dosing: The usual dose is ONE drop in the affected eye (or eyes) ONCE a day, in the EVENING. Use it at the same time every evening to get the best results. Do not use more than one drop per eye per day, as using it more often may actually make it less effective.
missed_dose: If you miss your evening dose, skip the missed dose and use your next dose the following evening at your regular time. Do not double up by using two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the bottle in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C) until you open it for the first time. After opening, you may store the bottle at room temperature between 36°F and 77°F (2°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Throw away the bottle 6 weeks after you first open it, even if there is still medicine left inside. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not wear contact lenses when you apply the drops — remove them first and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting. Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface to keep the solution sterile and prevent eye infections. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery right after using the drops if your vision is temporarily blurry. Avoid rubbing your eyes after applying the drops. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before using this medicine, as it may not be safe during pregnancy.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: sudden vision changes or vision loss; severe eye pain, redness, or irritation that does not go away; signs of an eye infection (discharge, swelling, or crusting); swelling or redness of the eyelids; changes in the color of your iris (the colored part of your eye) — this medicine may slowly and permanently darken your iris color; increased growth, darkening, or thickening of your eyelashes; any allergic reaction signs such as rash, itching, or difficulty breathing; or if your eye pressure does not seem to be improving at your follow-up appointments.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working within a few hours of your first dose, but you may not feel any different because high eye pressure usually has no noticeable symptoms. Your eye doctor will check your eye pressure at regular visits to make sure the medicine is working. It is important to keep using the drops every day, even if you feel fine. Do not stop using this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine may be harmful during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children under 18 years of age has not been established; consult your doctor. Older adults (65+): No dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but they should continue regular eye pressure monitoring. Contact lens wearers: Remove contact lenses before each dose and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting them, as the preservative in this medicine (benzalkonium chloride) can be absorbed by soft contact lenses and may irritate the eye. Kidney or liver disease: Limited information is available; talk to your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems.
